B("**Sales support and data entry:** follow the Upsell Playbook and IT’s Data Quality Checklist; no discretion of the required kind.")
P("**Federal conclusion.** The CEAS likely fails both duties prongs: its primary duty is not administrative work, and even the minority analytics work, as written, does not clearly involve discretion and independent judgment on matters of significance. We assess the probability that an exempt classification would be sustained in litigation as low. Because the role is staffed by 18 employees performing identical duties under a single job description, it would also be a natural candidate for conditional certification of a collective action under 29 U.S.C. § 216(b).", "j")

H(2, "G. Alternative Federal Exemptions Considered")
T(["Exemption", "Requirement", "Application"], [
    ["Executive, 29 C.F.R. § 541.100", "Primary duty management; customarily directs 2+ FTEs; hire/fire authority or weight", "No supervisory duties at all — **unavailable**"],
    ["Learned professional, § 541.301", "Primary duty requiring advanced knowledge in a field of science or learning customarily acquired by prolonged specialized instruction", "Degree preferred, not required; customer-service experience is the core requirement — **unavailable**"],
    ["Creative professional, § 541.302", "Invention, imagination, originality or talent in a recognized artistic field", "None — **unavailable**"],
    ["Computer employee, § 541.400", "Systems analysis, programming, software engineering", "End-user of Salesforce/Tableau — **unavailable** (see § 541.401)"],
    ["Outside sales, § 541.500", "Primary duty sales, customarily and regularly away from employer’s place of business", "All selling by phone/email/chat from workstation — **unavailable** (§ 541.502)"],
    ["Highly compensated, § 541.601", "Total annual compensation ≥ $107,432 plus one exempt duty customarily performed", "$55,200 — **unavailable**"],
    ["Retail/service commission, 29 U.S.C. § 207(i)", "Retail or service establishment; regular rate > 1.5× minimum wage; >50% of pay from commissions", "No commission — **unavailable** (and partial overtime exemption only)"],
    ["Combination, § 541.708", "Combining exempt duties of different exemptions", "Cannot combine exempt with non-exempt work — **unavailable**"],
], widths=[1.6, 2.6, 2.3])

# ---------- VI ----------
H(1, "VI. State-Law Analysis")
H(2, "A. California — Irvine (6 Positions): Non-Exempt as a Matter of Law")
P("**1. Salary.** An exempt administrative employee in California must earn a monthly salary equivalent to no less than two times the state minimum wage for full-time employment. Cal. Lab. Code § 515(a); IWC Wage Order 4-2001 § 1(A)(2)(g). With the 2025 statewide minimum wage of $16.50/hour, the floor is $68,640 per year ($5,720 per month; $1,320 per week). The CEAS salary of $55,200 is **$13,440 (19.6%) short**. The Grade 7 maximum of $62,000 is also short. Because the threshold is pegged to the minimum wage, it rises every January 1 (the Department of Industrial Relations announces the annual CPI adjustment in the prior summer), so any future exempt California position must be re-tested annually — exactly as the 2022 audit warned (\"An employee earning $54,000 or $55,000 annually ... would fall short of California’s exempt salary threshold\"). Thornbury did not analyze California at all and disclaimed state law; the grid’s California note for the CEAS row is blank. Mr. Polk’s March 17 statement that he \"trust[s] they’ve done their diligence on the geographic piece\" is contradicted by the letter itself.", "j")
P("**2. Duties — \"primarily engaged.\"** California requires that the employee be \"primarily engaged\" in exempt duties, meaning more than one-half of work time. Cal. Lab. Code § 515(e); Wage Order 4-2001 § 1(A)(2)(f), § 2. The test is quantitative and is measured by the employer’s realistic expectations and the work actually performed. __Ramirez v. Yosemite Water Co.__, 20 Cal. 4th 785 (1999). The Wage Order incorporates specified federal regulations (29 C.F.R. §§ 541.201–.205, .207–.208, .210, .215 as in effect in 2001) to define administrative work, but California does not adopt the federal flexible \"primary duty\" approach. See also __Harris v. Superior Court__, 53 Cal. 4th 170 (2011) (administrative/production dichotomy is not a dispositive test; analysis follows the Wage Order and incorporated regulations). With at most 25% arguably exempt time, the role fails by a wide margin.", "j")
P("**3. Consequences.** Irvine CEAS employees must receive daily overtime (1.5× after 8 hours/day and for the first 8 hours on the seventh consecutive day; 2× after 12 hours/day and after 8 on the seventh day), weekly overtime after 40, Cal. Lab. Code § 510; compliant meal periods (§ 512) and rest periods (Wage Order 4 § 12), with one hour of premium pay per day for each type of violation (§ 226.7); itemized wage statements showing hours and rates (§ 226); timely final pay (§§ 201–203). If a salaried-non-exempt structure is used, the salary is deemed to compensate only 40 hours and the regular rate is 1/40 of the weekly salary, § 515(d); the fluctuating-workweek method is not permitted in California. Misclassification exposure includes three-year Labor Code limitations (four years under Bus. & Prof. Code § 17208 for restitution), waiting-time penalties up to 30 days’ wages (§ 203), wage-statement penalties (§ 226(e)), and PAGA penalties (Lab. Code § 2699, as amended effective 2024, which reduces penalties for employers that take reasonable pre-notice compliance steps — another reason to fix this before hire).", "j")
H(2, "B. Oregon — Portland Remote Hub (4 Positions): Non-Exempt")
P("Oregon exempts bona fide executive, administrative and professional employees who meet the duties tests of the federal regulations and are paid a salary of at least the applicable Oregon minimum wage × 2,080 hours. ORS 653.020(3); OAR 839-020-0300(1)–(3). For the Portland metro region the minimum wage was $15.95/hour as of July 1, 2024 (annual floor $33,176), increasing to $16.30 on July 1, 2025 ($33,904); the CEAS salary clears this. The duties analysis, however, follows the federal regulations, and the role fails it for the reasons in Section V. Oregon employees must therefore receive overtime after 40 hours (ORS 653.261; OAR 839-020-0030), Oregon-compliant meal and rest periods (OAR 839-020-0050), and accurate itemized statements. Misclassification exposure includes unpaid overtime, statutory penalty wages of up to 30 days (ORS 652.150), civil penalties under ORS 653.055, and attorney fees. Because these employees work from home, the Company should confirm that each employee’s home is within the Portland metro boundary (which determines the applicable minimum-wage tier) and that remote timekeeping is in place.", "j")
H(2, "C. Texas — Austin (8 Positions)")
P("Texas has no state overtime statute; the Texas Minimum Wage Act defers to the FLSA for covered employers, Tex. Lab. Code ch. 62, and the Texas Payday Law governs pay timing. The federal analysis controls for Austin. Austin employees are within the Fifth Circuit, which has permitted the half-time (fluctuating workweek) method to compute damages for misclassified salaried employees in some circumstances (__Blackmon v. Brookshire Grocery Co.__, 835 F.2d 1135 (5th Cir. 1988)); this may reduce but does not eliminate exposure, and it is not a basis for classification.", "j")
H(2, "D. Location Summary")
T(["Location (positions)", "Salary test", "Duties test", "Result"], [
    ["Austin, TX (8)", "Federal $684/wk — met ($1,061.54)", "Federal primary duty / § 541.200 — likely fails", "**Non-exempt**"],
    ["Irvine, CA (6)", "CA $68,640/yr — **fails** by $13,440", "CA \"primarily engaged\" >50% — **fails** (≤25%)", "**Non-exempt as a matter of law**"],
    ["Portland, OR (4)", "OR $33,176 (→ $33,904 on 7/1/25) — met", "Federal duties tests via OAR 839-020-0300 — likely fails", "**Non-exempt**"],
], widths=[1.4, 1.8, 2.0, 1.3])

# ---------- VII ----------
H(1, "VII. Evaluation of the Thornbury Recommendation")
P("Thornbury’s benchmarking work is useful for pay-setting. Its classification recommendation, however, should be given no weight in the legal determination, for the following reasons:", "j")
N("**Self-disclaimed scope.** The letter states it \"does not constitute legal advice,\" addresses only federal requirements, is based exclusively on the job description, and recommends counsel review before implementation. It expressly flags that state thresholds may differ — yet the email chain treats it as having resolved the California question.")
N("**Wrong salary rule.** It relies on the vacated 2024 rule and miscasts __Texas v. DOL__ as pending; and its statement that the salary clears \"any\" standard is incorrect as to the $1,128 tier.")
N("**Facts not in the job description.** It attributes to the CEAS the design of \"custom\" dashboards, independent selection of metrics, direct reporting to senior leadership, and discretionary resolution of complaints \"beyond\" scripted protocols — none of which appears in, and several of which are contradicted by, the February 10 job description.")
N("**Legal error on primary duty.** It dismisses 40% customer service as \"incidental\" without addressing the § 541.700 factors, ignores the 20% clerical and 15% sales components, and never confronts the fact that 75% of the role is non-exempt.")
N("**No good-faith shield.** Reliance on a non-legal consultant’s opinion — particularly after counsel has raised contrary concerns — is not the kind of reliance that supports the good-faith defense to liquidated damages under 29 U.S.C. § 260, and it is not a written administrative ruling of the Wage and Hour Administrator under the Portal-to-Portal Act, 29 U.S.C. § 259. The 2022 audit memo specifically warned the Company of this.")

# ---------- VIII ----------
H(1, "VIII. Risk and Exposure Assessment")
H(2, "A. Willfulness and Liquidated Damages")
P("A violation is willful if the employer knew or showed reckless disregard for whether its conduct was prohibited. __McLaughlin v. Richland Shoe Co.__, 486 U.S. 128, 133 (1988). Willfulness extends the limitations period from two to three years, 29 U.S.C. § 255(a). Liquidated damages equal to the unpaid overtime are mandatory unless the employer proves both subjective good faith and objectively reasonable grounds, 29 U.S.C. §§ 216(b), 260. Here the written record already includes: (i) counsel’s 2022 reclassification of a near-identical Grade 7 hybrid role and explicit warnings about hybrid roles, pre-built reporting and consultant reliance; (ii) the COO’s February 12, 2025 email noting the role \"could go either way\" and questioning California compliance; and (iii) the GC’s March 28, 2025 email identifying the California salary shortfall and the 25% primary-duty problem and requesting a hold. An exempt classification adopted over this record would be very difficult to defend as non-willful.", "j")
H(2, "B. Illustrative Federal Overtime Exposure (18 Employees)")
P("Assumptions: regular rate $26.54 (=$1,061.54 ÷ 40), overtime rate $39.81; 48 working weeks per year; three-year willful period; liquidated damages doubling. These figures exclude California daily overtime, meal/rest premiums, waiting-time, wage-statement and PAGA penalties, Oregon penalty wages, plaintiffs’ attorney fees, and defense costs, any of which can equal or exceed the base wage figures. If the Fifth Circuit half-time method were applied to Austin employees, the Austin component could be roughly one-third of these amounts.", "j")
T(["Avg. OT hrs/week", "Per employee / yr", "18 employees / yr", "With liquidated (×2) / yr", "3-year willful total"], [
    ["2", "$3,822", "$68,788", "$137,576", "$412,727"],
    ["5", "$9,554", "$171,969", "$343,939", "$1,031,817"],
    ["10", "$19,108", "$343,939", "$687,878", "$2,063,634"],
], widths=[1.1, 1.3, 1.3, 1.5, 1.3])
P("By contrast, the incremental cost of classifying the role as non-exempt is limited to overtime actually worked (which can be controlled by scheduling and authorization policies) plus timekeeping administration — the same \"trivial\" cost the 2022 audit memo described.", "j")
H(2, "C. Employee-Relations and Business Considerations")
B("Employees whose duties and pay closely resemble the eliminated non-exempt Senior CSR (at $24.50/hour plus overtime) may compare notes; former Senior CSRs hired into CEAS roles would lose overtime eligibility under an exempt classification, increasing claim likelihood.")
B("The peak-season evening/weekend shifts contemplated in the job description make overtime foreseeable, increasing both exposure and the plausibility of a willfulness finding.")
B("Posting the role as exempt and later reclassifying 18 employees is more disruptive than posting it correctly now.")

# ---------- IX ----------
H(1, "IX. Recommendations")
H(2, "A. Immediate (Before the April 21 Posting / May 19 Start)")
N("**Classify the CEAS as non-exempt in all three locations.** Revise the \"FLSA Status\" fields in the Position Summary and Compensation tables of the job description; do not post the role as exempt. If the posting date cannot move, post only after this change is made.")
N("**Set compliant pay.** Recommended: an hourly rate of $26.54 (equivalent to $55,200 at 40 hours) with overtime at 1.5× (and California daily overtime/double time), budgeted for peak-season hours. A salaried non-exempt approach is permissible but in California the salary covers only 40 hours (Lab. Code § 515(d)); we recommend hourly pay for simplicity and uniformity. Confirm hourly rates exceed all applicable minimums (they do: CA $16.50; Portland metro $15.95, rising to $16.30 on July 1, 2025).")
N("**Timekeeping and policies.** Configure the position code with Lone Star Payroll Solutions as non-exempt; implement electronic timekeeping (including remote Portland employees and time spent on CRM, reports and after-hours email/chat); adopt a written overtime-authorization policy (while paying all overtime actually worked); implement California and Oregon meal/rest-period scheduling, attestation and premium-pay processes; ensure California wage statements comply with § 226; provide California Wage Theft Prevention Act notices (§ 2810.5) at hire.")
N("**Correct the file.** Have HR (not the hiring business unit or the consultant) correct comp grid v3.2: replace \"$844/wk per 2024 DOL rule\" with the operative $684/wk 2019 threshold throughout; correct the \"Pending Regulatory Note\" to reflect that the 2024 rule (including the $1,128 tier) was vacated; complete the California and Oregon notes for the CEAS row; and reflect non-exempt status. Document that the classification decision followed legal review.")
N("**Manager training.** Brief Mr. Polk, the Customer Experience Manager and Team Leads on non-exempt timekeeping, off-the-clock risk, and that \"exempt\" is a legal status, not a seniority level.")
H(2, "B. If the Business Needs an Exempt Analytics Function")
P("The cleanest path to preserving genuine analytics capability is structural, not a label:", "j")
B("**Split the role.** Create (i) a non-exempt customer-service/upsell role and (ii) a separate Customer Experience Analyst role whose primary duty — well over 50% of time, and verified in practice — is designing analyses, selecting metrics, building non-templated reporting, and making recommendations that affect product, warranty or retention policy, with real authority to recommend and some freedom from immediate supervision, reporting to an exempt manager.")
B("**Pay it as an exempt role.** Federal: comfortably above $684/week, with headroom for future rulemaking. California: at or above the current-year state floor ($68,640 in 2025; re-test every January), which would require a grade above Grade 7 (the Grade 8 minimum of $68,000 is itself below the California floor and is already flagged in the grid). Oregon: at or above the regional minimum-wage floor.")
B("**Validate after hire.** Conduct a documented duties audit (supervisor interviews, time study, observation) within six months, consistent with both the 2022 audit and Thornbury’s own recommendation.")
H(2, "C. Related Compliance Items")
B("**Marketing Coordinator.** Confirm that all three Marketing Coordinator incumbents shown in Grade 7 are being treated as non-exempt, consistent with the 2022 reclassification. If any are paid as exempt, correct prospectively and evaluate back-pay under privilege.")
B("**Annual classification review.** Implement the annual review recommended in 2022, including annual re-testing of California exempt salaries against the new minimum wage each January 1.")
B("**Regulatory monitoring.** Monitor any appeal in __Texas v. DOL__ and any new DOL salary rulemaking; a future federal increase could also affect other Grade 7 exempt roles (Logistics Coordinator, Inventory Analyst, Purchasing Specialist, Vendor Relations Coordinator), which should be duties-reviewed on their own merits.")
B("**Privilege.** Keep this analysis and any exposure modeling within the legal department; communicate the classification decision to the business as a decision, without forwarding this memorandum.")

# ---------- X ----------
H(1, "X. Conclusion")
P("The CEAS is a predominantly customer-service, clerical and inside-sales position with a minority, largely templated analytics component. It is non-exempt as a matter of law in California because it fails both the salary floor and the \"primarily engaged\" test, and it is very likely non-exempt under the FLSA (and therefore in Texas and Oregon) because its primary duty is not administrative work involving discretion and independent judgment on matters of significance. The Thornbury letter does not change that conclusion and, given the Company’s documented awareness of the risk, reliance on it would aggravate rather than mitigate exposure. We recommend classifying all 18 CEAS positions as non-exempt before the role is posted, and — if exempt-level analytics work is a genuine business need — creating a separate, properly scoped and properly compensated analyst role.", "j")
P("__Caveats: This memorandum is based solely on the five documents listed in Section III; no incumbents exist and no interviews or observation have been conducted. Statutory thresholds cited are those in effect for 2025 and change periodically (California and Oregon annually). Case citations and regulatory references should be cite-checked before this analysis is shared outside the legal department or relied upon in any proceeding.__", "j")

content.text:
Wrote a privileged FLSA and state-law classification memo for the CEAS role (18 positions in Austin, Irvine and Portland). It concludes the role is non-exempt everywhere: in California it fails the $68,640 salary floor and the more-than-50% exempt-duties test; federally (and so in Texas and Oregon) it likely fails the administrative duties test, since 75% of the work is non-exempt. It also explains why the Thornbury letter cannot be relied on, estimates willfulness and overtime exposure, and lists remediation steps. The file passed validate.py and opened cleanly when parsed back.
